newsitem.title: UK: Talisman gets OK to develop North Sea Ross field.
newsitem.headline: Talisman gets OK to develop North Sea Ross field.

text.p: Britain's Department of Trade and Industry Thursday gave Canada's Talisman Energy Inc. permission to develop its Ross North Sea oil and gas field.
The field, which lies about 50 miles northeast of St. Fergus in Scotland, has estimated recoverable reserves of 66 million barrels of oil and 20 billion cubic feet of gas.
The Ross development, operated by Talisman, comprises two blocks, and Talisman has more than a 50 percent interest in both blocks.

Oil from Ross will be exported by shuttle tanker from a floating production, storage and offloading vessel. Gas will be exported via a connection to the Frigg pipeline, the Department of Trade and Industry said.
First production is expected in the third quarter of 1998.
Calgary, Alberta-based Talisman said in April it was bolstering its North Sea activities through the acquisition of BHP Petroleum's 17.5 percent stake in two blocks adjacent to the Clyde field.
It also acquired Kerr-McGee Corp.'s assets in the North Sea, including an additional 25 percent stake in the Beatrice field and Nigg terminal.
